question: A 5-year-old boy with symptoms of possible meningitis is seen in an emergency department. Gram-negative diplococci and abundant polymorphonuclear leukocytes are observed in the Gram stain of the cerebrospinal fluid sediment. What microorganism does it suggest as a possible cause of the infection ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Gram-negative diplococci in Gram stain of CSF sediment -> Possible Neisseria meningitidis infection -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Abundant polymorphonuclear leukocytes in CSF sediment -> Suggestive of acute bacterial meningitis -> Possible Neisseria meningitidis infection -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: Symptoms of possible meningitis in a 5-year-old boy -> Gram-negative diplococci in CSF sediment -> Likely Neisseria meningitidis infection -> 90%
